confidence_notes: Restaurant meal and coffee anchors are based on aggregated cost-of-living web results. A citycost.org-style comparison gave a budget meal of about CHF 24, a mid-range three-course dinner for two of about CHF 116 and a cappuccino of about CHF 4.78. Another source put a three-course dinner at about CHF 40 per person. I nudged these up slightly for a July 2026 peak-season tourist town. The CHF-to-USD conversion assumes about 1.25 USD per CHF, which is my own estimate and not taken from a source. The beer search results were for 0.33 L or 0.5 L bottles, not a draft serving in a restaurant. The draft beer anchor is therefore a model estimate of about CHF 7.50 for a 0.5 L draft in a restaurant. The cocktail and wine searches found only scrambled hotel bar menus, with no usable aggregated prices. Cocktail (about CHF 17) and wine by the glass (about CHF 8.50) are therefore estimated from typical Swiss relationships to beer prices and are less certain. All four accommodation anchors are general-knowledge model estimates for July peak season, which is very high-demand in Interlaken. I did not search for accommodation or inspect any listings. FX: the RBA figure of 0.6720 USD per AUD for 2026-11-18 was confirmed only through secondary sites that cite RBA data. I did not read the RBA page directly, so check the official RBA page to confirm it.
comparable_city_reasoning: Interlaken is a small, very touristy Alpine resort town in the Bernese Oberland. Prices are broadly in line with Swiss city levels such as Bern and Lucerne, with a tourist premium on drinks and summer accommodation. It is comparable to Grindelwald, Zermatt and Lucerne for summer visitor pricing.
